lucas: heads-up — I ran a small sweep today of the kernel routing + page-aware prefetcher for GQA/MQA on the stripe cache layout. hitting a perf regression for short sequences (<=32) on a subset of kernels.

ajay: hmm, regression where exactly? end-to-end p99 or per-token?

lucas: per-token latency. baseline routing (static pick based on arch+seq) = ~2.8ms/token on A100 for seq<=32. new route w/ prefetch window and sequence-cut routing = ~3.5ms/token for same bucket.

maria: interesting, longer sequences improved?

lucas: yes — seq>512 got better: baseline 2.3ms/token -> new 2.1ms/token. so the prefetch helps when there's enough KV pages to amortize, but hurts tiny seqs.

perf-bot: quick profiling dump (roofline-lite):
```
cmd: bench_route --model=resnet-like --arch=A100 --seq=32 --layout=stripe
baseline: 2.8 ms/token
new-route(prefetch=window=64,block=256): 3.5 ms/token
allocs: +8% mem ops, +12% L1 thrashed
hotspots: kernel_dispatcher::choose_kernel(), kv_prefetch_loop()
```

ben: do we have a heatmap of kernel picks by seq? maybe routing picks a more expensive kernel for tiny seqs because prefetch heuristics bias toward block-friendly kernels.

ajay: can you dump the pick table? also which quant/path pair got chosen?

lucas: attached snippet from the run: kernel_picker chooses "pagelookup_stripe_v2" for seq<=32 because prefetch window>0 and it scores higher due to expected cache hits. but the actual access pattern for these short requests doesn't hit enough pages, so the extra prefetch loop costs more than the cache win.

maria: that sounds like a policy mismatch: scoring currently uses expected_page_hits = min(1.0, seq/block_sz * alpha) where alpha tuned for longer contexts. we should add a short-seq floor to avoid triggering prefetch-heavy kernels.

ben: proposal: add a quick early-exit in picker: if seq<=64 && batch_size<=8 -> force low-latency kernel (no prefetch). cheap guard.

ajay: +1. also we should try lowering prefetch window adaptively based on recent per-route page_hit ratio (moving average). if hit_ratio < 0.2 -> shrink window to 0.

lucas: I'll run two experiments: 1) picker guard (seq<=64 && batch<=8 -> fast path); 2) adaptive window based on per-route hit ratio with EMA(0.2). will run A/B on Dedicated pool tomorrow.

maria: please include the microbench harness commands and add the perf counters we looked at (L1 requests, L2 requests, dram reads).

lucas: will do. quick note: suspect also interaction with our batching heuristic — small bursts are coalesced into a single large batch shape which changes kernel scoring. I'll instrument batch shape distribution as well.

perf-bot: created perf ticket #PRF-4321 with initial data attached.

ben: thanks — if guard fixes it we should ship a hotfix branch and ramp on canary. otherwise we keep the adaptive window.

lucas: agreed. I'll post results in this thread after the runs. ping me if you want to join the bench window tomorrow morning (0900 PT). :rocket:
